svg.title: Predict the fragments before claiming a construct
svg.desc: A fictional linear1000-base-pair DNA molecule cut once at400bp yields400bp and600bp fragments whose lengths sum to1000. A single double-strand cut in a circular molecule instead opens one linear molecule of the original length. A separate stipulated staggered site is5′-G|AATTC-3′ aligned with3′-CTTAA|G-5′, producing complementary5′ overhangs after separation. Hydrogen-bond pairing can align compatible ends while ligase seals suitable covalent backbone nicks; neither operation invents an absent gene. This six-base sequence does not derive the independent1000bp map. Fragment,insert,orientation and sequence checks remain necessary before a functional construct claim.

g.text: Predict the fragments before claiming a construct
A length-conserving map and a separate staggered-cut sequence show different kinds of evidence.
Linear molecule: 1000 bp; one internal double-strand cut
Two fragments: 400 + 600 = 1000 bp. One cut in a circular molecule instead opens one linear piece.
A defined sticky-end example (rust marks show the two backbone cuts):
The two examples are separate: the short recognition site does not derive the 1000-bp fragment map.
Predict sites and fragments first; confirm insert presence, orientation and sequence after joining.
Opening DNA is not proof that the desired gene was isolated or that a construct is functional.
